transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-22
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Recording: yes (auto-transcript)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis + Priya (Redwood SEs), Dave (CTO - ZenCore), Sarah (Platform Eng), Ravi (Head of ML), Tina (Security)

Summary (auto):
Discovery focused on reliability, incident tolerance, and fallback policies across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private installs. ZenCore wants clear SLOs for latency/availability, proof points for multi-region failover, and security assurances for Private/VPC options. Next steps include pricing, tech deep-dive, and security questionnaire.

Topics: reliability, fallbacks, multi-region routing, SLA expectations, private deployment, KMS/keys, SOC2/audit logs

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros then we'll jump into reliability questions you sent over.
[00:09] Dave (ZenCore): Thanks, Maya. I'm Dave, CTO. Looking for how Redwood handles outages and what our options are for minimizing customer impact.
[00:16] Sarah: Yeah hi, Sarah, platform eng. We're mainly interested in production SLOs and how fallback policies work across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:23] Ravi: And I'm Ravi, ML. We have latency-sensitive endpoints for inference. We need to understand tail latency and how retries/fallbacks affect quality.
[00:33] Maya: Great. Luis is our SE — he'll go through traffic patterns, multi-region routing, and failover behaviors. Priya will touch on private/VPC/security.
[00:40] Luis (Redwood SE): Hi all. Quick high-level: Redwood supports Hosted (multi-tenant managed), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools per customer), and Private (VPC or on-prem). For reliability we use smart routing, region-aware failover, and model-variant fallbacks.
[00:56] Sarah: When you say region-aware failover, is that active-active or active-passive? What's the expected failover time?
[01:04] Luis: Good Q. For Hosted we typically run active-active across two regions for higher tiers; traffic is routed by latency and health. On a regional failure we fail traffic over within 10s to 30s for in-flight requests depending on the protocol (streaming responses might see longer reconciliation). We have canary checks and health probes.
[01:27] Dave: 10 to 30 seconds — that's promising. But how do you preserve session context / KV cache during failover? We rely on KV cache to keep costs down.
[01:36] Luis: Right — KV cache is per-serving node. For cross-region failover we maintain cache warmers, but there's inevitably a cold-cache penalty on a full failover. To mitigate, we do prefix caching and cached model variants; also we support sticky routing to preferred region for sessions where low P99 matters. Cold-cache tail latency tradeoffs are part of the SLA discussion.
[01:58] Ravi: Can you do model variant fallback — e.g., if the high-capacity 70b model isn't available we fall back to a quantized 7b with degraded latency/quality? How's that handled?
[02:08] Luis: Yes. Fallback policies are configurable. You can specify ordered fallbacks by model family, quantization, or performance tier. We run quality checks to ensure the fallback meets a minimum output quality. Apps can receive signals (via response metadata) when a fallback occurred.
[02:23] Sarah: Is that automatic or do we need to build logic client-side?
[02:26] Priya (Redwood): It's both. Redwood can auto-fallback based on capacity or latency guards. You can also opt for explicit client-side logic using the SDK to prefer specific variants. Many customers use server-side policy + app-level monitoring.
[02:37] Tina (Security): On outages, how are audit logs and request traces preserved, and are they available when traffic is routed to a different region or to Redwood Dedicated?
[02:47] Priya: Logs and traces are centralized into our observability pipeline. For Hosted, logs are retained per your plan; for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and push logs to your SIEM. During failover logs continue to be captured; cross-region routing preserves trace IDs so you can stitch sessions. There can be some timestamp skew if clocks differ.
[03:06] Dave: What's the SLA for Hosted vs Dedicated? We're looking for 99.9% or better for mission-critical endpoints.
[03:12] Maya: Hosted SLA varies by tier. Our enterprise Hosted plan offers a 99.9% uptime SLA for inference endpoints; Dedicated comes with a higher customization path and can include a 99.95% commitment depending on capacity commits and architecture. Private is subject to your infra — we provide operational runbooks and a managed control plane option.
[03:33] Dave: Do you provide credits for downtime? How's the SLA measured — per-route, per-model, or global?
[03:40] Maya: SLA is measured at the endpoint/route level (the specific model+config). Credits are pro-rated based on the downtime window per standard terms. We can show sample SLA doc after this call.
[03:50] Ravi: Curious about degraded modes: if model quality drops after fallback, do you provide any automated rollbacks to previous stable model?
[03:57] Luis: We have rollout policies: canary, A/B, and automatic rollback based on quality metrics derived from your evals or Redwood's monitors. If a fallback is worse than your threshold, the system can pause the fallback and route to a different variant or a read-only cached response, depending on policy.
[04:18] Sarah: For Dedicated, if a physical GPU node fails, what's the behavior? Is there automatic rescheduling?
[04:24] Luis: Dedicated pools are multi-instance; the orchestrator will reschedule to available nodes. If capacity is constrained, we can route overflow to Hosted (if you enable cross-tier fallback) or serve degraded model variants. Rescheduling is fast for stateless requests, but warm-up for long KV caches can add seconds.
[04:42] Dave: Overflow to Hosted — that sounds like a security concern for some customers. Can we opt out?
[04:47] Priya: Absolutely — cross-tier fallback is opt-in. Many regulated customers disable Hosted overflow and instead configure burst capacity or on-prem fallback.
[04:55] Tina: For Private deployments, do you still get the Redwood control plane? Does that create any phone-home vectors?
[05:02] Priya: We offer two Private modes: a fully air-gapped on-prem option with no control plane traffic back to Redwood, and a hybrid VPC option where the control plane communicates over customer-managed tunnels for updates/metrics. Everything is configurable and we support KMS integrations and enterprise firewall rules.
[05:20] Tina: Good. We need documented attestations for SOC2 and encryption at rest.
[05:24] Maya: We'll include SOC2 / ISO docs and KMS integration guides in the follow-up.
[05:29] Sarah: Can you quantify failover latency in worst case? We need estimates for SRE runbooks.
[05:35] Luis: For Hosted active-active, failover detection + routing is typically under 30s. For Dedicated within same region with autoscaling, reschedule is under 20s for new stateless tasks, but cold-cache penalties can add 1-8s on p95/p99 depending on sequence lengths and model size. Cross-region, plan for 10-60s depending on DNS or LB TTLs — we can provide exact numbers per region topology.
[06:00] Ravi: How about streaming sessions — do you preserve partial tokens or drop the stream?
[06:05] Luis: Streaming is trickier. If a node fails mid-stream we try to buffer and resume; in practice short interruptions are possible and clients should be built to handle reconnects. We send metadata to indicate interruption and whether a retry will restart the completion or resume.
[06:21] Dave: On quantization/fallback: can we set floor quality — e.g., no fallback to < 80% accuracy on our eval suite?
[06:29] Priya: Yes, you can tie fallback gates to evaluation thresholds. Redwood Optimize can manage model selection recommendations and quality regression alerts based on your evals.
[06:39] Sarah: Licensing/commit: if we do Dedicated reserved capacity, do we get dedicated network isolation?
[06:43] Maya: Yes, Dedicated offers isolated pools and network controls. For extra isolation we recommend Private VPC or on-prem. Dedicated can also be deployed in customer VPCs depending on the contract.
[06:55] Tina: Audit trail requirements: we need immutable audit logs for admin actions and key rotation evidence. Is that available?
[07:03] Priya: Yes. For enterprise plans we support immutable audit logs export and HSM/KMS integration; we provide rotation logs and key access logs as part of compliance packages.
[07:12] Dave: What tools do you provide to simulate outages so we can test our app behavior?
[07:16] Luis: We provide a chaos-testing guide, simulated failover endpoints, and a benchmark harness you can run to emulate region loss and capacity constraints. We'll share the benchmark spreadsheet and runbook link.
[07:27] Sarah: Great. For capex planning, show us how the cost behaves under frequent fallbacks — e.g., if we route to smaller quantized models a lot, it saves tokens but impacts latency.
[07:36] Maya: We'll include a cost model spreadsheet showing per-token cost, per-inference overhead, and the economics of fallback. We can model your qps and peak windows once you share traffic patterns.
[07:46] Ravi: Any limitations for private on-prem? E.g., specific GPUs or kernel versions?
[07:51] Priya: There's a supported hardware matrix. We support major NVIDIA cards and some AMD/others via specific runtimes. We'll attach the support matrix. On-prem requires a small agent and orchestration piece; we can run air-gapped as noted.
[08:05] Dave: Is multi-region Private supported? We have EU + US presence and prefer a private option in both regions.
[08:11] Luis: Yes, you can deploy Private clusters per region and configure smart routing via your LB or via Redwood's control plane for hybrid. Cross-region private routing is possible with peering and controlled tunnels.
[08:22] Tina: Encryption in transit — are you supporting customer-provided certificates?
[08:26] Priya: Yes, we support customer certs, mutual TLS, and custom CAs for private installs.
[08:33] Sarah: For monitoring, do you expose token-level latency breakdowns? We need to know where time is spent.
[08:38] Luis: We provide token-level time breakdowns (fetch, kv cache, attention compute, kernel time) in the Console and via traces for enterprise plans.
[08:46] Dave: If we need an SLA guarantee for P99 latency, is that feasible?
[08:50] Maya: P99 latency SLAs are possible on Dedicated with reserved capacity and warm caches; we should run a benchmark with your workload to validate and include SLOs in the contract.
[08:59] Ravi: Ok let's talk about the benchmark — what do you need from us?
[09:02] Luis: A representative prompt set, typical sequence lengths, qps, burst profiles, and any critical time windows. Also your eval set so we can set fallback quality gates.
[09:14] Ravi: We'll send that.
[09:16] Maya: Quick recap and next steps?
[09:18] Dave: yes please.
[09:19] Maya: We'll send Dedicated pricing and a cost model spreadsheet by Friday (2026-09-24). Luis will schedule a 2-hour technical deep dive to walk through Private deployment and multi-region diagrams for the week of 2026-09-29. Priya will include security docs: SOC2, KMS integration, and supported hardware matrix. ZenCore to send qps and evals.
[09:37] Sarah: Sounds good. Also Tina will share a baseline security questionnaire.
[09:41] Tina: Yup, sending it today.
[09:44] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links to the benchmark spreadsheet and the chaos-testing runbook.
[09:50] Dave: Appreciate it. Bye.

End of transcript.
